retraction_of_the_previous_round.what_was_claimed: the residual class for the goal is 2 statements, priced at log2(2) = 1 question of the user, with 0 runs of any of three machines able to pay it
retraction_of_the_previous_round.what_it_was: a theorem about suites that begin at reset: with the probe count starting at 0 and every atom changing it by at most one, created_once is the same sentence as monotone and final count == 1, at every depth and for every machine
retraction_of_the_previous_round.what_is_true_now: one real action from one real pre-state separates the two statements in both directions, at the price of a prefix of length <= 2 and zero questions of the user
retraction_of_the_previous_round.why_it_matters: the ceiling was the first state of the run, which is the experimenter's convention and not a property of tar, coreutils or SQLite; a measured limit is only a limit until the convention that produced it is named

P5.was: the first implementation added a condition the declared criterion did not contain: that every atom executed by an experiment exits zero
P5.is: the declared criterion is what is checked -- every pre-state reproduced exactly, nothing fabricated -- plus a stronger one: no witness may be a failed action
P5.why: GNU tar --delete of a member that is absent and GNU mv of a name that is absent exit non-zero and do nothing: that is the tool being real, not a fabrication. The first implementation therefore failed on a condition it had invented, and the honest repair is to check the condition that matters

P2 and P3.was: a pre-state experiment separates the pair
P2 and P3.is: a pre-state experiment that changes the probe count separates the pair (strengthened, not relaxed: the first run already met the weaker version)
P2 and P3.why: the first run showed the pair separates even on a no-op from a state holding one copy. That is true and worth reporting, but it is degenerate: the claim worth making is that a run which changes the count separates them, and a no-op cannot be mistaken for evidence about what an action does

probes_run_before_the_criteria_were_writ: a two-action run of FS_A1;FS_A4 was executed while reading the code, and it made the count rise twice, so it does not separate the pair: this checked the theorem's premise
no pre-state experiment (replay a prefix, then act) was run before P1-P6 were written

declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.P1: the pair disagrees on zero reset-started runs and every atom moves the count by at most one, so the equivalence is forced and is not evidence about the world
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.P2: a pre-state experiment separates the pair in both directions on at least two machines
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.P3: the separation costs at most a prefix of length 2 plus one action and zero questions
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.P4: the pair's class is 1 on the widened suite and 2 on the standard one
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.P5: every experiment either reproduces its recorded pre-state or is excluded
declared_acceptance_before_the_receipt_r.P6: zero model calls, zero stored parameters, every run executed

P2_the_pair_separates_in_one_substantive.why_the_other_direction_cannot_be_substa: on a run with no decrease and unit steps, the final count is start + the number of increases; `single_copy` and not `created_once` forces increases = 0 and final = 1, so start = 1 and nothing may change. A substantive witness for that direction is not missing, it is impossible, and that impossibility is the whole reason the previous round's pair could not be separated from reset

P3_the_price_is_actions_and_not_question.previous_round_priced_it_at: log2(2) = 1 question of the user, 0 runs able to pay it

degenerate_that_changed_nothing.why_it_counts: a run from a state that already holds one copy separates the pair even when nothing happens, which is exactly why a suite whose runs all begin at zero can never see the difference

tarball_duplicate_member_probe.what_was_done: delete the seed member, append the probe content as `seed`, then append it again as `seed` -- two members, same name, same bytes
tarball_duplicate_member_probe.reading: the member list holds two entries named `seed`, but extracting by name prints both bodies, so each row carries the doubled text and no row equals the probe content: the count goes from one to zero, not to two. On this machine a second copy is not observable at all, which is why TARBALL cannot offer the substantive witness -- its own reader is the limiting part

discovery_where_the_substantive_directio.what_it_means: a machine can only offer the substantive witness if one of its atoms adds a copy from a state that already holds one; on TARBALL the only such route is a second member with the same name, and that machine's reader folds the two members into one row, so its own observation cannot see the second copy -- on that machine the reader is the limiting part

secondary_evidence_full_grammar_term_set.note: widening adds runs and therefore behaviours; the number reported here is the goal's class over the whole grammar, which can fall for the pair's reason and rise nowhere

theorem.statement: on any suite whose runs begin with zero copies of the probe content, if every atom changes that count by at most one, then created_once[c] and monotone[c] and final:count[c]==1 are the same function of the run
theorem.how_to_falsify: find an atom that creates two copies of one content in a single action, or a suite that starts with a copy already present; the second is what this round does on purpose

limits: pre-states are those reachable in at most two real actions and capped per machine; the closure of the state space is not enumerated
the theorem's premise is measured on the states exercised, not proved for every state
widening the suite adds behaviours, so it costs statements elsewhere: the goal's class over the full grammar is reported for both suites rather than only the flattering one
the synthesis side of coding is untouched: this says what an edit would have to satisfy, not how to compose the edit
